title: Trio SDKs: lean reauth flow, streaming hints, and ergonomic connector contracts
author: Jordan Kim
release_notes:
- Introduce lightweight reauth handoff for long-lived streams across Python/TS/Go SDKs
- Add per-sdk streaming 'hints' API to express desired backpressure/heartbeat guidance
- Bump versions: python -> 1.14.0, typescript -> 1.27.3, go -> 1.8.2
- Telemetry: emit reauth/refresh events for easier debugging
description: Summary: This PR converges three ergonomic changes across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs: (1) a lean reauth handoff path for long-lived streaming consumers that reduces auth chatter and avoids full stream restart on refresh, (2) an explicit streaming hints surface that allows callers to provide lightweight backpressure and heartbeat guidance to the runtime, and (3) small connector contract cleanups for parity across SDKs so downstream clients see consistent types and behaviors. Motivation: Customers running production streaming workloads reported spikes during token refresh windows and found SDKs diverged in how they signaled intended consumer pacing. This caused inconsistency in server-side batching and observability. The goal here is to reduce the auth restart surface, give application authors a low-friction hint API for streaming behavior, and keep the three SDKs aligned so documentation and examples remain valid. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1284) - [x] Implement Python, TypeScript, Go adapters - [x] Add unit + integration tests for reauth handoff and hints - [x] Add end-to-end streaming test that simulates token rotation - [x] Update CHANGELOGs and bump SDK versions - [x] Update minimal examples in /examples/streaming Changes & Commits: commit 1: sketch reauth handoff protocol and types (python/ts/go) commit 2: implement reauth state machine and fallback (python) commit 3: implement StreamingHints API and wire into client (ts) commit 4: implement go connector contract and tests commit 5: unify names, add telemetry events, bump versions Tests & CI: - Local unit tests added for all three SDKs testing: reauth path, retained-kv cache during reauth, stream iterator resume semantics, and hints being respected by client mock. - Integration test: end-to-end stream between local test server and each SDK that performs token rotation mid-stream. - CI: all stages passed on first run except a lint failure in TS which was fixed in follow-up commit; final CI status: pass Files touched (high-level): - sdk/python/redwood/streaming/reauth.py - sdk/python/tests/test_stream_reauth.py - sdk/typescript/src/stream/streamingHints.ts - sdk/typescript/tests/streaming-hints.spec.ts - sdk/go/stream/connector.go - sdk/go/stream/connector_test.go - examples/streaming/simple_hints_example.(py|ts|go) - CHANGELOGs and package manifests Notable diffs (illustrative snippets): - Python: added ReauthHandoff class with two public methods: provide_refresh_token(new_token) and try_resume(stream_context). Implementation uses a short-lived lease token exchange; avoids re-opening the websocket when successful. - TypeScript: exported interface StreamingHints { preferredChunkMillis?: number; heartbeatIntervalMs?: number; preferredBatchSize?: number } and client accepts hints in Client.stream(hints?). Hints are purely advisory but emitted as telemetry. - Go: simplified connector signature: NewConnector(ctx, opts ConnectorOptions) where ConnectorOptions now contains StreamHints and ReauthCallback func(ctx context.Context, refreshedToken string) error Compatibility & ergonomics notes: - These changes are additive: StreamingHints are optional and default to legacy behavior. Reauth handoff will attempt non-invasive resume first, and fall back to full reconnect only when resume fails, preserving existing semantics for consumers that do not opt-in. - The Go connector signature change is backward-compatible because ConnectorOptions is a new struct; calls that supply nil opts will continue to work. Review conversation (selected): - Aisha Patel (reviewer): "Overall this is great; two asks: (1) tighten the timeout on the lease exchange to 3s, (2) emit an explicit telemetry event when resume fails with reason code to reduce noise during incident triage." - Jordan Kim (author): "Addressed: lease timeout now 3s, added telemetry event 'stream.resume_failed' with reason tags. Added tests for telemetry emission." - Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "TS API looks good but please add a small inline example in the JSDoc showing a heartbeat hint usage." - Jordan Kim: "Added JSDoc and updated examples directory." - Marisol Vega (reviewer): "Go tests flaky on CI for connector_test; suggest increasing test harness jitter and add deterministic seed." - Jordan Kim: "Added deterministic seed and removed a 10ms sleep; CI run stable afterwards." Edge cases & decisions: - We intentionally avoided a synchronous reauth API to keep SDK ergonomics simple; the handoff is callback/lease-based and intentionally small surface area. - We considered an optimistic token-swap where the client would push tokens mid-request; deferred because server-runbook still needs to support idempotent in-flight token acceptance. - Managed to keep the payload change minimal for the wire protocol: a small 'resume' control message with lease id and optional last-offset. Observability: - New telemetry events: stream.renew_requested, stream.renew_succeeded, stream.resume_attempt, stream.resume_failed (with reason tag), streaming.hints.applied - Updated debug logs at INFO: 'attempting resume', 'resume accepted', 'resume rejected: reason' Version bumps & packaging: - Python: SDK bumped to 1.14.0 (published wheel candidate) - TypeScript: SDK bumped to 1.27.3 (npm tag next) - Go: SDK bumped to 1.8.2 (module tag v1.8.2) Migration notes for integrators: - Most callers will see no change. To use the new features: pass a StreamingHints object into streaming entrypoint, and, for long-lived streams, implement a lightweight callback that accepts reauth lease tokens if you want to participate in non-disruptive refresh. - If you rely on connector constructors in Go with custom options, validate nil-handling for ConnectorOptions but no change required for nil usage. CI artifacts & performance: - Microbench: resume path reduces median restart latency from ~1200ms to ~140ms in the happy-path resumed case in our local harness. - Memory: negligible change. - CI artifacts attached in PR: e2e-stream-rotation-20260215.log and per-sdk unit test reports. Merge & release: - Merged via squash on 2026-02-15 after all reviewers approved. - Changelogs updated in each SDK package and release PRs queued to publish artifacts next release window. Follow-ups & open items: - ENG-1302: server-side acceptance of optimistic mid-request token swap (tracked separately) - Add an advanced guide to the Console docs showing troubleshooting steps for stream resume failures - Consider a server-side telemetry roll-up to summarize resume failure rates per-customer Performance telemetry dashboards will be added next sprint. If any SDK maintainer prefers a revert of the Go connector change we can isolate that into a follow-up; however current CI and downstream tests in staging passed.
